name: Arum
confidence_why: One first-hand description of the tone system, checked against the source; 4 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

tone_statements.citation: Siegel, Wolfram. 2025. Alumu-Tesu (Alumu Təsu) [alphabet and pronunciation chart with notes, in German; 'Compiled by Wolfram Siegel 2025-07-16']. Published on Omniglot, 'Alumu language and alphabet' (S. Ager ed.), www.omniglot.com. 1 p.
tone_statements.quote: 5. Alumu-Tesu ist eine Tonsprache mit fünf Tönen: – a) einem Hochton [-˥] (gekennzeichnet mit einem Akut ›◌́‹); – b) einem Mittelton [-˧] (unbezeichnet); – c) einem Tiefton [-˩] (gekennzeichnet mit einem Gravis ›◌̀‹); – d) einem steigenden Ton [-˩˥] (gekennzeichnet mit einem Hatschek ›◌̌‹); – e) einem fallenden Ton [-˥˩] (gekennzeichnet mit einem Zirkumflex ›◌̂‹). Daneben gibt es auch zahlreiche Mischformen. Die Kennzeichnung der Töne ist nicht zwingend.
tone_statements.translation: 5. Alumu-Tesu is a tone language with five tones: a) a high tone (marked with an acute); b) a mid tone (unmarked); c) a low tone (marked with a grave); d) a rising tone (marked with a hacek); e) a falling tone (marked with a circumflex). Besides these there are also numerous mixed forms. Marking of the tones is not obligatory.
tone_statements.summary: 3 levels H M L + rising, falling contours (secondhand restatement of Blench & Kato: 3 level tones, glides = sequences).

tone_statements.citation: Blench, Roger & Barau Kato. 2012. The Təsu language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment (printout June 11, 2012). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 32 pp.
tone_statements.quote: 3.3 Tones Təsu has three level tones, and numerous glide tones that arise from sequences of level tones. The basic conventions are as follows; High ʹ Mid Unmarked Low ˋ Rising ˇ Falling ˆ

sources.note: Index page only; confirms no further Alumu/Tesu description beyond the Tesu wordlist draft.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2010b/2012. The Toro language of Central Nigeria and its affinities (Toro wordlist) -- sister Alumic language Atoro [tdv], same format; may carry a parallel tone/stress note usable as group-level evidence only
sources.note: Closest related description by the same author; would show whether Blench says anything about stress for any Alumic language (not downloaded: different glottocode, toro1234-type variety, not Arum itself)

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, David Onoja, Innocent Jonah, John Muniru & Samuel Eju. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Arum (Alumu-Tesu) [aab] and Atoro [tdv] Languages of Nasarawa State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-048. SIL International. 60 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey with 348-item wordlists; sec. 8.5 treats vowel correspondences Arum vs Atoro; Appendix F (p.36): 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Sec. 3 confirms the only prior linguistic work is Maddieson (1972) short wordlist and Blench's 1999/2003 wordlists (Blench 2004, 2010a,b).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Barau Kato. 2012. The Təsu language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment (printout June 11, 2012). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 32 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 Phonology (pp.5-6) gives vowels, consonants and 3.3 Tones: 'Təsu has three level tones, and numerous glide tones that arise from sequences of level tones' with tone-marking conventions; the word 'stress'/'accent' does not occur anywhere in the document.

tone.quote: 3.3 Tones Təsu has three level tones, and numerous glide tones that arise from sequences of level tones. The basic conventions are as follows; High ʹ Mid Unmarked Low ˋ Rising ˇ Falling ˆ
tone.says: Three level tones (high, mid, low); rising and falling glides are analysed as sequences of level tones. Preliminary wordlist transcription of the Təsu (Chessu) variety; nothing said on stress.
